newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal's premier confident of winning test vote.
newsitem.headline: Nepal's premier confident of winning test vote.

text.p: Nepal's government said on Monday it would defeat a communist-backed no-confidence motion despite the defection of some rebel deputies from the ruling coalition.
"We will face the motion and we are confident that it will be defeated," Parliamentary Affairs Minister Narahari Acharya told Reuters in the capital of Kathmandu.

On Sunday, 11 breakaway deputies of the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), holding a crucial balance of power in parliament, announced they were withdrawing support for Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba's 15-month-old coalition government.
Seven of 13 RPP ministers resigned from Deuba's 46-member government.
Acharya said Deuba had called the ministers to verify their signatures. "He will take a decision (on their resignation) after meeting the ministers," he said.

The three-party coalition has controlled 108 seats in the 205-seat lower house, where Deuba's Nepali Congress party has 86 lawmakers. RPP has 19 seats and Nepal Sadbhavana Party (NSP) has three members.

But the opposition United-Marxist-Leninist (UML) party, with 87 deputies, has joined the 11 breakaway RPP lawmakers and asked King Birendra to convene a special parliamentary session to take up a motion against Deuba.
There was no response yet from the palace to the request.

UML officials claimed they had the support of 102 members, including two independent deputies who vote with the UML but not three members of the leftist Nepal Workers' and Peasants' Party (NWPP) who vote independently.
Currently, there are 200 sitting members of parliament. But rules require a majority of the house's 205 total seats -- or 103 votes -- to topple a government.
The breakaway faction was led by the RPP's parliamentary leader, Lokendra Bahadur Chand, who was criticised by party president Surya Bahadur Thapa.
Chand on Sunday accused Deuba's Nepali Congress of harassing party workers and breaking an agreement with coalition partners. He did not elaborate.
The UML, which accuses Deuba's government of corruption and inefficiency, has offered to back a new government headed by the RPP's Chand.
In March, six RPP ministers resigned from the government, but they quickly patched up their differences with the government in time for Deuba to survive a no-confidence motion.
